{{Short description|Scottish chemist and inventor (1939-2004)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2017}}
{{Use British English|date=January 2017}}
'''Bryan Barnet Molloy''' (30 March 1939 – 20 May 2004) was a Scottish-French chemist, known notably for helping to invent the [[antidepressant]] ''Prozac'', a name for [[fluoxetine]]. ''Prozac'' was introduced in 1988, and has been the world's leading antidepressant.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Domino EF|title=History of modern psychopharmacology: A personal view with an emphasis on antidepressants|journal=Psychosomatic Medicine|volume=61|issue=5|pages=591–8|year=1999|pmid=10511010|doi=10.1097/00006842-199909000-00002|url=http://www.psychosomaticmedicine.org/cgi/pmidlookup?view=long&pmid=10511010}}</ref>

==Early life==
He was born in [[Broughty Ferry]], in the east of [[Dundee]]. He received a BSc degree in Chemistry in 1960 from the [[University of St Andrews]], gaining a PhD in 1963.

==Career==
He moved to the US in 1963, working on research at three universities for three years, including [[Imperial College London]] and Columbia University (with Gilbert Stork, organic chemistry). In his professional career, he researched the [[neurotransmitter]] [[acetylcholine]], and its effect on the heart.

[[File:Mechanism of Prozac.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mechanism of prozac]]

===Prozac===
He worked with [[David T. Wong]] and [[Klaus Schmiegel]]. [[Tricyclic antidepressant]]s had been introduced in the 1950s, and further antidepressants included [[monoamine oxidase inhibitor]]s (MAOIs); these had side-effects. In 1971, Wong and Molloy went to a lecture in [[Indianapolis]] given by [[Solomon H. Snyder]], a neuroscientist at [[Johns Hopkins University]]. This gave them a method to test new compounds similar to [[antihistamine]]s found by Molloy, one being fluoxetine.<ref name="Fuller">{{cite web|title=Ray W. Fuller, David T. Wong, and Bryan B. Molloy|url=https://www.sciencehistory.org/historical-profile/ray-w-fuller-david-t-wong-and-bryan-b-molloy|website=Science History Institute|accessdate=21 March 2018 }}</ref>

Fluoxetine hydrochloride (3-aryloxy-3-phenylpropylamine, an aryloxyphenylpropylamine), the first of the [[selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor]]s (SSRIs), was inventor in 1972, and made public in 1974; work had begun with [[Robert Rathbun]] in 1970. Other well-known SSRIs would be [[sertraline]] (''Zoloft'') from [[Pfizer]], and [[paroxetine]] (''Paxil'' or ''Seroxat'') from GSK. Fluoxetine is on the [[WHO Model List of Essential Medicines]].

He later worked on [[cardiovascular disease]] and [[cardiac arrhythmia]], and [[phenethylamine]]s as antidepressants. He retired in 2001.

==Personal life==
He married Kay Koch in 1971. They lived on a farm in [[Indiana]]. He had a [[Pilot licensing and certification|pilot's licence]]. He became a US citizen in 1990. He died in 2004, aged 65, in [[Marion County, Indiana]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bryan Molloy, Ph.D. Obituary & Funeral {{!}} Indianapolis, IN |url=https://www.lifestorynet.com/obituaries/bryan-molloy-ph-d.3287 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.lifestorynet.com |language=en}}</ref> He was listed in the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] on 18 September 1999 at [[Akron, Ohio]].
